trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
The line must go up: left is number 14, which comes later.
Going up would force the line onto number 4 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Going down would force the line onto number 14 before its turn; going up leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
I can't rule out up or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going left would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Going up, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,6). So the line goes right.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Going left, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,7). So the line goes up.
Cell (2,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going left would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes down.
The line must go down: left is number 9, which comes later.
Going left would leave number 9 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down would leave number 9 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up.
Going up would strand number 9: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going down would strand number 11: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
The line must go right: down is number 13, which comes later.
Going down would cut off the bottom-left corner (6 cells); going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.

Going left would leave both cell (5,1) and cell (7,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down would leave both cell (7,1) and cell (7,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
